title: Obstructions

D0.outcome: Explains an obstruction as a low-value piece or pawn that blocks lines, easier to remove when it is the enemy's.

D1.outcome: In a given position, names the obstructions of both sides and the line each blocks.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides whether to remove an enemy obstruction, leave it, or use it, and removes his own blocked pawn by placing a piece under its protection.

D3.outcome: Predicts when an obstruction helps the attacker (a pawn sacrifice delaying castling; a queen as blockader).

misconceptions: Obstruction and blockade are two names for the same thing.
conditions: Enemy obstructions are easier to remove than your own blocked pawn.
contrasts: Obstruction helps the attacker (Morphy's pawn sacrifice that delays the enemy king from castling).
Using one vocabulary for obstruction and blockade.
An obstruction on a line that leads nowhere.
